pack.license: Images: public domain (US government works). Catalog data: CC0-1.0.
pack.description: US coin design types with public-domain reference images from the United States Mint and the Smithsonian National Numismatic Collection, verified via Wikimedia Commons.

items.title: Lincoln cent, Union Shield reverse (2010-present)

obverse: File:2025 Lincoln cent obverse, uncirculated, Philadelphia mint.jpg

items.notes: Circulation pennies were last struck for commerce in 2025.

items.title: Lincoln cent, Memorial reverse (1959-2008)
items.notes: 1982 cents exist in both bronze (3.11 g) and zinc (2.5 g); weighing tells them apart.

items.title: Lincoln cent, Wheat reverse (1909-1958)

obverse: File:1909-S VDB Lincoln cent obverse transparent background.png

items.notes: Key dates include 1909-S VDB, 1909-S, 1914-D, 1922 (no D) and 1931-S. 1943 cents are zinc-coated steel.

items.title: Lincoln cent, 1943 zinc-coated steel
items.notes: Silvery color and attracted to a magnet. A copper-colored 1943 cent is either a rare error or plated; have it authenticated.

items.title: Lincoln Bicentennial cent: Birth and Early Childhood in Kentucky (2009)
Lincoln Bicentennial cent: Formative Years in Indiana (2009)
Indian Head cent, oak wreath and shield reverse (1860-1909)
items.notes: Key dates include 1869, 1872, 1877 and 1909-S.

items.title: Jefferson nickel, forward-facing portrait (2006-present)
items.notes: The Monticello reverse is also used on 1938-2003 nickels, which have a left-facing profile.

items.title: Jefferson nickel, profile portrait (1938-2004)
items.notes: 1942-1945 'war nickels' with a large mint mark above Monticello contain 35% silver (0.0563 troy oz).

items.title: Westward Journey nickel: Ocean in View (2005)
Buffalo nickel, Type 2 'line' reverse (1913-1938)
items.notes: Dates wear off easily. Key coins include 1913-S Type 2, 1916 doubled die, 1918/7-D, 1921-S, 1926-S and 1937-D three-legged.

items.title: Buffalo nickel, Type 1 'mound' reverse (1913)
items.notes: The bison stands on a raised mound; on Type 2 it stands on a flat line with 'FIVE CENTS' recessed below.

items.title: Roosevelt dime (1946-present)
items.notes: Dimes dated 1964 and earlier are 90% silver (0.0723 troy oz); 1965 and later are copper-nickel clad.

items.title: Winged Liberty Head ('Mercury') dime (1916-1945)
items.notes: Key dates include 1916-D, 1921 and 1921-D. Full split bands on the reverse fasces add value.

items.title: Washington quarter, Bicentennial drummer boy reverse (1776-1976)

obverse: File:1976 United States Bicentennial quarter obverse.jpg

items.notes: Struck in huge numbers; circulated examples are worth face value. 40% silver versions were sold in collector sets (S mint mark).

items.title: Standing Liberty quarter (1916-1930)
items.notes: Dates on 1916-1924 coins were raised and often wore away. 1916 and 1918/7-S are key dates.

items.title: Susan B. Anthony dollar (1979-1981, 1999)
items.notes: Often confused with quarters because of its size and reeded edge; the 11-sided inner border is distinctive.

items.title: Morgan dollar (1878-1904, 1921)
items.notes: The mint mark sits below the wreath on the reverse; CC (Carson City) coins usually carry a premium. Key dates include 1889-CC, 1893-S and 1895 (proof only).

items.title: Peace dollar (1921-1935)
items.notes: 1921 coins are high relief; 1928 and 1934-S are key dates.
